summary: A website for uploading Need for Speed mods. Users can upload, browse, and manage NFS game mods. User authentication via Internet Identity is being added so mod creators can manage their own uploads.

existing_features.title: Build a mod browsing/listing page as the homepage. Display all uploaded mods in a responsive grid of cards. Each card shows the mod title, game name, category badge, author, upload date, and download count. Include a search bar to filter by title or game, and a category filter dropdown.

Build a mod upload form page accessible via an 'Upload Mod' button in the navigation. The form should collect: mod title, description, target NFS game (select from a predefined list: Underground, Underground 2, Most Wanted, Carbon, ProStreet, The Run, Rivals, Heat, Unbound), category (Cars, Tracks, Textures, Gameplay, UI, Other), author name, and a file input for the mod file. On submit, call the backend uploadMod method and show a success or error notification.

Build a mod detail page reachable by clicking a mod card on the listing page. Display full mod details: title, description, game, category, author, upload date, and download count. Include a 'Download' button that calls incrementDownloadCount on the backend and triggers the file download. Include a 'Back to Mods' navigation link.

Apply a dark, high-octane racing visual theme throughout the site. Use a dark charcoal/near-black background with neon yellow-green (#C8FF00 or similar) as the primary accent color, evoking street racing aesthetics. Use a bold, modern sans-serif typeface for headings and a clean readable font for body text. Cards should have a dark surface with subtle glowing borders on hover. The navigation bar should be dark with the site logo and accent-colored call-to-action buttons. Apply this theme consistently across all pages.

Render the generated static image assets from frontend/public/assets/generated. Use the hero banner image on the homepage above the mod listing grid, and the NFS Mod Garage logo in the navigation bar.

Add a Login/Logout button to the navigation bar in Layout.tsx that uses the existing `useInternetIdentity` hook. When logged out, show a 'Login' button styled with the neon accent color that triggers Internet Identity authentication. When logged in, show the user's abbreviated principal and a 'Logout' button.

Protect the mod upload page and form: if the user is not authenticated, redirect them to the homepage or show a prompt to log in via Internet Identity instead of the upload form. When authenticated, the upload form should use the authenticated actor (from `useActor`) so the caller's principal is recorded. Remove the manual 'author name' field or pre-fill it from identity context, since the principal is now stored on the backend.

Create a 'My Mods' page at route `/my-mods` that is only accessible when the user is authenticated. The page fetches and displays all mods belonging to the logged-in user by calling `getModsByOwner` with their principal. Each mod entry in the list shows the mod title, game, category, upload date, and a 'Delete' button. The 'Delete' button calls `deleteMod` on the backend (using the authenticated actor) and refreshes the list on success. Show a confirmation prompt before deletion. Add a 'My Mods' navigation link in the nav bar that is only visible when logged in.

Add an optional preview image file input to the mod upload form on `ModUploadPage.tsx`. When a user selects an image file, convert it to bytes and include it in the `uploadMod` backend call. Show a thumbnail preview of the selected image before submission. Image upload should be clearly marked as optional.

Update `ModCard.tsx` to display the mod's preview image at the top of each card when available. Fetch the preview image using `getModPreviewImage`. When no preview image is available, display a styled fallback placeholder (e.g., a dark panel with the NFS Mod Garage logo or a generic car silhouette icon). The image should be displayed in a fixed-aspect-ratio container to keep the grid uniform.

Update `ModDetailPage.tsx` to prominently display the mod's preview image near the top of the page when one exists. Fetch the preview image using `getModPreviewImage`. When no preview image is available, display a styled fallback placeholder. The image should be shown at a larger size than on the mod cards.

Update `ModListingPage.tsx` to use the new hero banner image asset (`hero-banner.dim_1920x600.png`) as the full-width hero banner above the mod listing grid, replacing any previously referenced hero banner image filename.

In `frontend/src/components/Layout.tsx`, remove the logo/banner image currently displayed in the top-left of the navigation bar and replace it with the bold custom text 'NFS MODS HUB'. Style the text using the existing neon accent color (#C8FF00 or the CSS variable equivalent), the Barlow Condensed bold typeface, and uppercase lettering to match the dark high-octane racing theme. The text should link to the homepage ('/') just as the logo did.

Enhance the 'NFS MODS HUB' text in the navigation bar (`frontend/src/components/Layout.tsx`) with a neon glow effect using CSS text-shadow with the neon accent color (#C8FF00). Ensure the Barlow Condensed bold typeface is applied. Optionally add a subtle pulsing or static glow animation to make the branding visually striking.

Apply neon glow styling to other key accent elements across the site (e.g., the 'Upload Mod' button, active nav links, download buttons, category badges, and card hover borders) using CSS box-shadow or text-shadow with the neon accent color (#C8FF00). Define reusable Tailwind utility classes or CSS custom properties for neon glow effects in `frontend/src/index.css` or `frontend/tailwind.config.js` so the effect is applied consistently.

new_feature_requests.summary: Create a backend data model and actor methods for NFS mods. Each mod entry should store: title, description, game (e.g., NFS Most Wanted, NFS Underground), category (e.g., Cars, Tracks, Textures, Gameplay), author name, upload timestamp, download count, and file metadata (name, size in bytes). Expose methods: uploadMod (create), listMods (paginated), getModById, incrementDownloadCount, and deleteMod.

Add Internet Identity authentication: login/logout in nav bar, protected mod uploads with principal stored per mod, and a My Mods page where logged-in users can view and delete only their own uploads.

Update the backend Motoko actor to store the uploader's principal (caller) with each mod entry. Add a query method `getModsByOwner(principal)` that returns only mods belonging to that principal. Update `uploadMod` to record the caller's principal as the mod owner. Update `deleteMod` to enforce that only the mod owner (matching principal) can delete their own mod; return an error variant if the caller is not the owner.

Add optional mod preview image upload to the submission form. Store the image in the backend with the mod entry. Display the preview image on mod cards in the listing grid and on the mod detail page, with a fallback placeholder when no image is provided.

Update the backend Motoko actor to add an optional preview image field (as a Blob or byte array) to the mod data model. Update the `uploadMod` method to accept an optional preview image parameter and store it alongside the mod entry. Add a query method `getModPreviewImage(modId)` that returns the stored preview image bytes for a given mod ID.

Replace the existing hero banner image on the homepage with the user-provided NFS-style banner (red Mitsubishi Lancer racing through a canyon at night), displayed full-width above the mod listing grid.
Add a neon glow effect and custom font styling to the 'NFS MODS HUB' nav text and key accent elements to make them visually pop.
